Problem 1 of 5

You have an idea, but nothing is built yet

Every month without a product is a month handed to your competitors. And a wrong technical choice at the start costs you for years: an app to rewrite, payments that fail, a team blocked by its own architecture.

What I do

  • I start from your real need and scope a first useful version
  • I design the architecture: API, database, web and mobile apps
  • I build what makes the product live: payments, notifications, real time
  • I publish to the stores and ship to production, with the tests

Proof

    Utando

    Logistics platform designed from scratch: Node.js / Fastify API on PostgreSQL, 3 Expo apps and a React back office, MTN MoMo and Orange Money payments, a payouts ledger, background jobs and geolocation.

    Snow Volican

    Events platform built alone: FastAPI on PostgreSQL, React front end, Stripe payments, Sentry on front and back end.

Problem 2 of 5

Your app breaks in production

Every release becomes a gamble. Payment fails on a Friday night, your customers notice before you do, and the team spends the week fighting fires instead of moving forward.

What I do

  • End-to-end tests on the paths that bring money: signup, cart, payment
  • Docker images built by GitHub Actions, identical in test and production
  • A release checked before the switch, with instant rollback
  • Sentry on front end and back end, to see the error before the customer does

Proof

  • Freelance · live

    Adsquid

    344 Playwright tests on signup, cart and Stripe / PayPal payment. 10 production releases with blue-green deploys and instant rollback.

  • Freelance · 2025

    Snow Volican

    Zero-downtime deploys: several instances behind Nginx, health checks, one instance updated at a time, triggered by GitHub Actions.

  • WebPackSolution · live

    290 test files covering login, two-factor authentication, roles and client identity checks.

Problem 3 of 5

You inherited code nobody understands

Every change breaks something else. The original developer is gone, the announced migration was never really done, and your roadmap moves at the pace of regressions.

What I do

  • I audit what exists: what works, what breaks, what's missing
  • I turn the audit into a migration plan in small, verifiable steps
  • I put tests in place as a safety net before touching the core
  • Every fixed bug becomes an automatic rule so it never comes back

Proof

  • Taking over an existing platform

    Adsquid

    Audited 10 modules, 563 columns and 262 business rules: only 9 columns were actually migrated. The audit became the migration plan to Payload CMS and Next.js on PostgreSQL.

  • Freelance

    Epiltech

    Shop and training courses migrated from Prisma to Payload on PostgreSQL, with the whole infrastructure self-hosted on Docker Compose and daily backups.

Next stepIt works, but it's slow?

Problem 4 of 5

Your users wait, then leave

Three seconds too many, a network drop, a stuttering screen: users don't complain, they uninstall. And you never find out.

What I do

  • I measure before and after every fix, to prove the gain
  • I cut what the app redraws and what it downloads
  • I design for unstable networks and small phones
  • I set up real time properly: WebRTC, sockets, STOMP

Proof

  • Sole developer of the TV and mobile apps

    StackZ and One2All TV

    A remote-control move redraws 2 cards instead of about 14, measured with Flashlight. WebRTC live video, STOMP real time, Picture-in-Picture, published on 3 stores.

    stackz.gg (opens in a new tab)

  • Kevmax · telemedicine

    Docta

    Flutter app with real-time chat over sockets and a map of nearby practitioners.

    doctaapp.fr (opens in a new tab)

Next stepAnd when your messages don't arrive?

Problem 5 of 5

Your notifications don't arrive, or they annoy

A driver misses a ride, a payment is confirmed without anyone knowing, or the app sends so many messages that your users turn everything off.

What I do

  • Reliable push notifications on Android and iOS
  • Android channels and per-type preferences
  • Scheduled reminders with a frequency cap
  • Email and calendar when push isn't the right channel

Proof

  • Push notifications · OneSignal

    Utando

    Push on the driver, partner and traveler apps and the back office, with Android notification channels.

  • Personal product

    Karreer

    Push notifications with cron-scheduled reminders and a frequency cap, so users are never flooded.

  • WebPackSolution

    Real-estate CRM

    Scheduled visits with email notifications and a calendar invite, and a first contact required within 4 hours for every lead.

Next stepHow I work

Method

A predictable method for unpredictable projects

  1. 01

    Understand

    The real need, the users, and what success means

  2. 02

    Audit or design

    The existing code if there is any, otherwise the simplest architecture that holds

  3. 03

    Break it down

    Concrete user paths and verifiable steps

  4. 04

    Build and test

    Small tested pieces, every bug becomes a test

  5. 05

    Ship to production

    Docker, checks before the switch, rollback ready

  6. 06

    Monitor and hand over

    Sentry, documentation, a clear handover
